A [[shooting guard]], Edwards played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]] and was selected with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] by the Timberwolves in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. He is a four-time [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]], a two-time [[All-NBA Second Team]] selection, and won a gold medal on the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 U.S. Olympic team]].{{cite web |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/anthony-edwards_1954701 |title=EDWARDS Anthony |work=[[Paris 2024 Olympics]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240823055638/https://olympics.com/en/paris-2024/athlete/anthony-edwards_1954701 |archive-date=August 23, 2024}} Edwards finished his high school career at [[Holy Spirit Preparatory School]] in his hometown of [[Atlanta]], Georgia, where he was rated a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best players in the 2019 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he earned [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and [[USA Today All-USA high school basketball team|''USA Today'' All-USA first team]] honors. He committed to play college basketball for Georgia, becoming the highest-rated recruit to do so, and was named [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] after his freshman season with the team. ==Early life== Edwards spent his early life in [[Oakland City, Atlanta|Oakland City, Atlanta, Georgia]].{{Cite web |last=Krawczynski |first=Jon |date=October 23, 2023 |title=At just 22, all eyes are on Anthony Edwards as two cities stand behind him |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4947669/2023/10/23/anthony-edwards-minnesota-timberwolves-oakland-city/ |access-date=May 23, 2024 |website=The Athletic}} When he was three years old, he was given the nickname "Ant-Man" by his father. For much of his childhood, Edwards played [[American football|football]] in the [[running back]], [[quarterback]], and [[cornerback]] positions.{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Ricky |title=The origin story of high school basketball's 'Ant-Man' |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2019/1/15/18139281/anthony-edwards-basketball-recruiting-nba-draft |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=April 25, 2019 |date=January 15, 2019}} He played youth football for the Atlanta Vikings and became one of the best [[Pop Warner Little Scholars|Pop Warner]] running backs in the country by age 10.{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Ryan |title=Anthony Edwards Is Ready For the Next Level |url=https://www.slamonline.com/the-magazine/anthony-edwards-story/ |newspaper=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |access-date=April 25, 2019 |date=April 12, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Westerholm |first1=Tom |title=Anthony Edwards, No. 4 prospect in 2019, honed toughness, intangibles as a football player |url=https://bluearticles.com/anthony-edwards/ |website=[[The Republican (Springfield, Massachusetts)|The Republican]] |access-date=April 25, 2019 |date=January 21, 2019 |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513155549/https://bluearticles.com/anthony-edwards/ |url-status=dead}} Edwards switched his focus to basketball because he "thought it looked more fun" after watching his brothers play the sport. He often played basketball with his brothers at their grandmother's house. Entering ninth grade, he began training with Justin Holland, a former [[college basketball]] player for [[Liberty Flames basketball|Liberty]] and an Atlanta-based basketball trainer. ==High school== Due to his success with the Atlanta Xpress 15-under [[Amateur Athletic Union]] team, Edwards was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] in 2016.{{cite web |last1=McDonald |first1=Dan |title=Four-star SG Anthony Edwards making moves |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/four-star-sg-anthony-edwards-making-moves |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=April 26, 2019 |date=March 12, 2017}} He began playing high school basketball for [[Therrell High School]] in Atlanta as a member of the 2019 class.{{cite web |last1=Krohn |first1=Adam |title=Life ordinary for nation's top basketball prospect Edwards |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/life-ordinary-for-nation-top-prospect-edwards/lEvjBtck7UXhdmNko50nDL/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=April 26, 2019 |date=January 15, 2019}} In early January 2017, Edwards transferred to [[Holy Spirit Preparatory School]] in Atlanta and [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2020 class. He made the move in an effort to improve his academic performance, since Holy Spirit Preparatory had "small class sizes and support to help that."{{cite web |last1=Neysmith |first1=Horace He was drawn to Georgia because two of his favorite players, [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Victor Oladipo]], had been coached in college by head coach [[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]].{{cite web |last1=Polacek |first1=Scott |title=5-Star SG Anthony Edwards Commits to Georgia; Potential No. 1 for 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2808426-5-star-sg-anthony-edwards-commits-to-georgia-potential-no-1-for-2020-nba-draft |publisher=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=November 26, 2019 |date=February 11, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Anthony Edwards | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Atlanta|Atlanta, GA]] | highschool = [[Holy Spirit Preparatory School|Holy Spirit Prep]] (GA) | feet = 6 | inches = 4 | weight = 205 | 40 = | commitdate = February 11, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 96 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Georgia 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Georgia Bulldogs Recruiting Class | rivals school = georgia | scout s = | espn schoolid = 61 | 247 overall = 1 | rivals overall = 3 | espn overall = 4 | access-date = January 29, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Anthony Edwards Georgia 2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Edwards in 2020]] On November 5, 2019, Edwards made his debut for the Georgia Bulldogs, recording 24 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 steals in a 91–72 win over [[Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball|Western Carolina]]. It was the most points by a Georgia freshman debutant since [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Basketball Hall of Fame]] inductee [[Dominique Wilkins]] in 1979.{{cite news |title=Edwards debuts with 24 points as Georgia beats Catamounts |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169800 |access-date=November 6, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} On November 26, he scored a season-high 37 points, including 33 in the second half, and posted six rebounds, four steals, and three [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] in a 93–85 loss to third-ranked [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] at the [[2019 Maui Invitational Tournament|Maui Invitational]]. top scorer on his team and among freshmen nationally. He earned second-team All-SEC and [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|SEC Freshman of the Year]] honors.{{cite press release |url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |access-date=March 10, 2020}} Edwards collected SEC Freshman of the Week accolades four times during the season, the most in program history.{{cite magazine |last1=Jackson |first1=Jordan |title=Anthony Edwards Named SEC Freshman of the Year |url=https://www.si.com/college/georgia/news/anthony-edwards-named-sec-freshman-of-the-year |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 24, 2020 |date=March 10, 2020}} He was also one of five finalists for the [[Jerry West Award]], which recognizes the top collegiate [[shooting guard]].{{cite web |title=Georgia's Edwards finalist for Jerry West Shooting Guard award |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/georgia-edwards-finalist-for-jerry-west-shooting-guard-award/fJITgXuu9YwXUBcNuF20AM/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=March 24, 2020 |date=March 3, 2020}} On March 20, 2020, in the spring of his freshman year, Edwards declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] as one of the most touted prospects in his class. He signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining college basketball eligibility.{{cite web |title=No. 1 prospect Anthony Edwards of Georgia declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28931229/no-1-prospect-anthony-edwards-georgia-declares-nba-draft |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=March 24, 2020 |date=March 20, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2020–present)=== ====2020–21 season: All-Rookie honors==== The [[2020 NBA draft]] was delayed by five months due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. In November 2020, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] selected Edwards as the No. 1 overall pick on draft night.
